title: How to use the site
lead: The catalogue of fonds and documents, information on services, branches and regional history — and how to use it all.

site.title: What is on the site
site.text: The main sections. They are also in the top menu.

catalog.label: Online catalogue
catalog.text: Fonds, inventories, case files and documents; open digital copies can be viewed on the site.

services.label: Services
services.text: How to get an archival certificate, paid services, the reading room, legal acts.

history.label: Regional history
history.text: Themed collections, online exhibitions, a timeline and a calendar of memorial dates.

about.label: About the archive
about.text: History, management and structure, news, contacts.

branches.label: Branches and map
branches.text: Addresses, contacts and directions to the head archive and the branches.

structure.title: How the catalogue is organised
structure.text: Documents are described level by level: each level sits inside the one before it. The archive code is built the same way.

archive.label: Archive
archive.text: The institution that keeps the fonds: the head archive or a branch.

fund.label: Fond
fund.text: All the records of one organisation, institution or person.

inventory.label: Inventory
inventory.text: A list of the fond's case files for certain years or on one subject.

case.label: Case file
case.text: A folder of documents on one matter: a year's orders, correspondence, a personal file.

document.label: Document
document.text: A single order, letter, photograph or map, with its date, code and, where available, a digital copy.

search.title: How to search and filter
search.text: You can search in plain words. The search allows for typos and different spellings of names.

query.title: Enter a query
query.text: The name of an organisation, a surname, an event, a place or a code, in the search box at the top of any page.

filters.title: Narrow the results
filters.text: In the catalogue, pick a fond, period, document type or topic. The filters are kept in the page address.

open.title: Open the record
open.text: The record shows the code, the dates, the place of storage and the access status of the digital copy.

fund.label: Fond, inventory, case file
fund.text: The numbers of the fond, inventory and case file, if you already know them.

period.label: Period
period.text: The decade, year or exact dates of the document.

type.label: Document type
type.text: Order, minutes, photograph, map, newspaper and others.

topic.label: Topic
topic.text: Subject tags, such as an enterprise or a locality.

branch.label: Unit
branch.text: The head archive or the branch where the document is kept.

language.label: Language
language.text: The language the document is written in.

copy.label: Digital copy
copy.text: Show only documents that have a copy.

search.filtersText: Filters narrow the results by the document's details. They can be combined.

materials.title: What materials are published
materials.text: The site holds descriptions and open copies. Materials with restricted access are shown only as a record with the access conditions.

funds.label: Archival fonds
funds.text: The list of fonds with numbers, titles, years of the documents and former names of organisations.

personal.label: Personal fonds
personal.text: Records of personal origin: the fonds of individuals and families.

documents.label: Documents
documents.text: Orders, minutes, letters, photographs, maps and drawings, audio and video recordings.

exhibitions.label: Online exhibitions
exhibitions.text: Exhibits with captions, a source and image zoom.

memory.label: Great Archive of Memory
memory.text: Themed collections, biographical notes and a timeline of the region.

calendar.label: Calendar of memorial dates
calendar.text: Historical dates of the region for 2022–2026.

materials.searchText: One search box across all published materials.

cipher.title: How to read a code and a record
cipher.text: The code is the document's address in the archive. It is made up of the numbers of the fond, the inventory, the case file and the document. Give the code to the archive staff and the file will be found faster.
cipher.exampleLabel: An example code, part by part
cipher.note: The letter in a fonds number is part of the number; write it together with the digits.

code.label: Code
code.text: The full reference of the document: fond, inventory, case file, number.

place.label: Fond, inventory, case file
place.text: Links to the catalogue levels the document belongs to.

date.label: Date
date.text: The date or period of the document; an inexact date is given as it appears in the description.

type.label: Type and language
type.text: The kind of document and the language it is written in.

sheets.label: Sheets
sheets.text: The size of the document in sheets.

storage.label: Place of storage
storage.text: The head archive or the branch that keeps the original.

access.label: Access status
access.text: Whether the digital copy can be viewed on the site.

access.title: Access statuses of digital copies
access.text: A document's description and its file are published separately: the record may be open while the copy is not.

open.label: Open
open.text: The copy can be viewed on the site.

restricted.label: Restricted access
restricted.text: The copy is not provided on the site. The access conditions are in the record; ask the archive for details.

closed.label: Closed
closed.text: The copy is not published. Ask the archive about the access procedure.

needs_review.label: Access to be confirmed
needs_review.text: The right to publish is being checked. Until a decision is made, the copy stays closed.

access.notice: The server checks the right to a file every time it is opened: a closed copy cannot be obtained by a direct link, through search or through the archive assistant.

next.title: Where to go next
next.faqText: Short answers about the catalogue, access, branches and the site.
next.assistantText: Answers questions with links to the materials it found.
next.readingRoomText: Opening hours, how to prepare for a visit, and the rules for working with documents.

faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.lead: Short answers about the catalogue, access to copies, branches and the site itself.

more.title: Did not find an answer?
more.contactsText: Phone numbers, e-mail and opening hours of the archive.

readingRoom.title: Reading room
readingRoom.lead: In the reading room, the archive's documents are consulted on site. This page gives the opening hours, how to prepare for a visit, and the rules.

more.funds: Find a fond in the catalogue
more.certificate: Need a certificate rather than access to files?
more.certificateText: You apply for an archival certificate on eGov.kz; there is no need to come to the reading room.
more.fundsText: Fonds number, years covered and former names of organisations.

prepare.title: How to prepare for a visit

find.title: Find the fond in the catalogue
find.text: Write down the fond number and the codes of the files you need: with them the staff will find the documents faster.

call.title: Call the archive
call.text: Check where the files are kept, in the head archive or a branch, and when you can work with them.

come.title: Come during opening hours
come.text: The reading room of the head archive is open on weekdays; the hours are given on this page.

rules.title: General rules
rules.onsite: Documents are consulted on site, in the reading room.
rules.care: Follow the preservation requirements: do not mark the documents or fold the sheets.
rules.staff: The reading room staff decide how files are issued and how work is organised; follow their instructions.
rules.photo: Whether you may photograph or copy documents, and what you may bring with you, is set by the reading room regulations; ask the staff.

regulation.title: Reading room regulations
regulation.text: The use of archival documents is governed by the Rules for the acquisition, storage, registration and use of documents of the National Archival Fonds (Order No. 215 of 9 August 2023).
